Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

This is the no-Bookshelf ablation: no cross-domain fish-control research shelf
is provided. Base controller proposals only on the task contract, current and
inherited guidance, sampled solver results, inherited optimizer logs, and
current rollout evidence. Do not search for or reconstruct the omitted shelf
from neighboring configurations or repository history.

I’ll first read the workspace contract and the required multi-wake visual-signal skill, then inspect the current rollout and inherited evidence before touching the policy. I’ll keep all work inside this Phase 2 workspace and won’t consult the omitted research shelf.

The visual-first skill applies because the sampled evaluations include wake keyframes. Its workflow requires anchored comparison of the best finite run with the most informative failure, cross-checked against metrics and diagnostics; I’m following that before any candidate edit.

The four current sampled rollouts are all finite successes, so there is no current failure sheet to compare. I’ll use the best run against the replicated parent anchor, then inspect the most informative inherited regression available in the assigned optimizer logs; I won’t invent a failure classification that the evidence does not support.

The evidence supports promotion, not extrapolation: increasing only posterior steering share from `0.60` to `0.65` preserves the compact wake route while improving arrival, mean distance, relative upstream propulsion, and total effort. I’m recording that diagnosis before changing the policy, as required by the visual-first skill.

The policy now promotes the exact evaluated `0.65` posterior-share result and changes no other executable parameter. I’m distilling its reusable boundary into the experience bank: it is a closure/propulsion improvement with a modest load and per-time effort tradeoff, not evidence for monotone extrapolation.

I’ve completed the required policy, notes, and durable lesson updates. I’m now invoking the prescribed non-CFD checker: semantic guidance provenance, lightweight Julia contract execution, and workspace-boundary validation.

The first prescribed check found a rendered-workspace metadata defect: `README.md` marks the same guidance parent twice, so the checker cannot identify exactly one assigned parent. The contract says to repair checker failures; I’ll remove only the duplicate parent marker, leaving the assigned parent unchanged, then rerun.

The policy contract command could not start because `julia` is absent from this workspace’s executable path; the candidate itself did not fail. I’ll check the environment for an installed Julia binary, then run the exact lightweight assertion if one is available.

No Julia binary exists anywhere inside the Phase 2 workspace, so the runtime assertion is environment-blocked. I’m compensating with the strongest in-scope verification available: executable-code identity against the already evaluated winning sample, plus an explicit parameter-reference/schema audit; the semantic and boundary checks already pass.

Completed exactly one multi-wake candidate:

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_2d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:8) promotes the evaluated `tail_steering_gain=0.65` winner.
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1) records the visual diagnosis and hypothesis.
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:133) adds the evidence-backed applicability and falsification boundary.

Guidance and boundary checks pass. Parameter-schema audit passes, and executable code matches the evaluated winning sample. The Julia runtime assertion could not run because Julia is not installed in the environment. No CFD was run.
